input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The cycle-detection guard (`seen` set) was removed from the `__cause__` traversal loop. A cyclic exception cause chain now makes the loop spin forever.
- rationale: Trigger: an exception whose `__cause__` chain loops back, e.g. `a.__cause__ = b; b.__cause__ = a`, where neither cause matches `exception_cause_types`. The loop never reaches `None` and never returns. Impact: the retry predicate hangs, so the retried call never completes or fails.
critique: The finding describes the same defect as the label: the `__cause__` traversal lacks a cycle guard, so a cyclic cause chain never reaches None and the retry predicate spins forever. Both name the same trigger (mutually causing exceptions) and the same impact (the caller hangs).
